A Delta Airlines Boeing 767-400 on behalf of US Transportation Command, registration N836MH performing flight DL-8957 (Callsign CMB-542) from Frankfurt Hahn (Germany) to Kuwait (Kuwait), was enroute at FL330 about 70nm southsoutheast of Tirana (Albania) about to enter Greek Airspace at 19:10L (16:10Z) when the crew did not establish contact with Greek Air Traffic Control.

As result two Greek F-16 fighter aircraft were scrambled and departed their airbase at 19:28L intercepting the Boeing about 20 minutes later about 25nm southeast of Santorini (Greece), the crew of the Boeing finally reacted and communication was restored at about 19:50L. TBH, having worked with death records for a number of years, it's really hard to tell when someone has died. Death records are maintained by the 50 states in varying formats and with differing rules, and combining those records into a national Master Death Index (MDI) is a long laborious process. Joining any set of patient records to the MDI requires a significant amount of statistics and probability, as names change, SSNs and birthdates can be entered incorrectly, letters and digits are transposed, etc. Add to that a certain amount of fraud surrounding deaths and continuing benefits to the survivors and you can see that it's a messy business where mistakes are easy. A 1% error rate is actually pretty good considering the messy data. What is NOT good is how the VA and the Social Security Administration handle those cases where people have mistakenly been declared dead. It's an ugly process and no one at either agency is held accountable for finding and fixing these mistakes.
